title: Customer SLO briefs and weekend upgrade template bank
summary: A practical collection of short-form SLO/SLA briefings and customer-facing maintenance/upgrade message variants, paired with Terraform module annotation recommendations and a lightweight preflight checklist for private (VPC/on-prem) tenants. Designed for SRE and customer success to quickly compose tenant-specific notices and terraform change notes.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a template bank and quick-reference for communications and infra annotations used when scheduling upgrades or maintenance windows for private-deployment customers (VPC and on-prem). It pairs: 1) short SLO/SLA impact briefs; 2) three customer-facing message variants (concise, operational, executive); 3) pager / incident escalation blurb; and 4) terraform module comment conventions and preflight checklist items to include in commits/PR descriptions.

How to use:
- Pick an SLO brief that matches the targeted impact level (informational / degraded / degraded+rollback risk).
- Choose a message variant optimized for the recipient (developer contact vs. technical ops vs. executive sponsor).
- Attach the preflight checklist and the terraform annotation example to the PR that triggers the change.
- If a rollback or mitigation is likely, use the "degraded+rollback" SLO brief and include the "fast rollback" communication template.

SLO/SLA brief (1-2 sentences each):
- informational: "Planned maintenance: non-disruptive package upgrade scheduled. No expected impact to request success rates or latency SLOs. If you see an issue, contact support@redwood.example and include tenant id {{tenant_id}}."
- degraded: "Planned upgrade may cause short-lived request errors (<=5% additional error rate) and transient latency spikes. We expect SLO impact for up to 30 minutes. We will monitor and notify when complete."
- degraded+rollback-risk: "Planned upgrade has a non-negligible risk of rollback due to dependency changes. We may temporarily reroute requests to fallback model variants to preserve availability; expected SLO deviation up to 1 hour if rollback is required."

Customer-facing notice templates
- Concise (developer contact):
Subject: Planned maintenance: Redwood private deployment ({{window_start}} UTC)
Body: Hello {{contact_name}},
We will perform a planned maintenance window on {{window_date}} starting at {{window_start}} UTC and ending by {{window_end}} UTC. Expected impact: minimal; brief latency spikes possible. No action required. If you experience issues, open a support ticket or reply to this email with tenant id {{tenant_id}}.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops

- Operational (SRE/infra audience):
Subject: Scheduled upgrade: runtime + quantization patch ({{window_date}}, {{window_start}} UTC)
Body: Hi {{ops_contact}},
Scope: rolling upgrade of inference runtime across reserved nodes in your VPC. Steps: drain replicas, apply patch, warm KV cache, validate smoke tests (generation, embeddings). Expected visible effects: transient 5-10% increased 5xx errors on the drained node, latency spikes up to +200ms on in-flight requests. Mitigation: routing to dedicated fallback pool; automatic rollback if 90% smoke tests fail after warmup phase. Contact: on-call SRE, Pager duty: {{pd_link}}.

- Executive (product/CS sponsor):
Subject: Brief: Planned maintenance for private deployment ({{window_date}})
Body: Hello {{sponsor_name}},
We have a planned maintenance window on {{window_date}} to deploy performance and security updates. We expect nominal customer impact and will mitigate with staged rollouts and automated fallbacks. We will send a completion summary after the window.
Thanks,
Customer Success / Engineering

Fast rollback / outage template:
Subject: URGENT: Rolling back upgrade for tenant {{tenant_id}} ({{timestamp}} UTC)
Body: Summary: We observed regression in model responses and elevated error rates after the upgrade. Rolling back to prior runtime snapshot ({{release_tag}}). Estimated restoration time: 15-30 minutes. Impact: service will be available, requests may be delayed during rollback. Postmortem ETA: 72 hours.

Preflight checklist (include in PR description and comms):
- Confirmed backup of KV cache and model artifacts (s3://redwood-private/{{tenant_id}}/backups/{{date}})
- Smoke tests: generation (happy path), embeddings (cosine similarity workflow), auth flow, billing ping
- Resource capacity check: GPU pool headroom >= 20%
- Canary run plan: % of shard traffic (default 10%) and rollback gate thresholds (e.g., error_rate > 2% for 5m)
- Notification plan: at T-72h, T-24h, T-2h, T+15m, T+24h
- Runbook link included: CON-3421

Terraform annotation recommendations (short conventions to include in module/PR):
- In the module vars and README, add a "maintenance_notes" arg for operator-facing comments, e.g.:
  // maintenance_notes: "Upgrade route: v1.4.2 -> v1.5.0; requires kv-cache rebuild; expect 20% spool CPU during warmup"
- Tag changes with tenant metadata in module locals when applicable:
  // terraform tag example: { "tenant_id" = "{{tenant_id}}", "planned_window" = "2025-01-20T02:00Z" }
- PR title convention: "private-deploy: tenant={{tenant_id}} upgrade v1.5.0 window={{window_date}}"
- Add a checklist block in PR body that mirrors preflight checklist; CI should fail PR if critical smoke tests are not present.

Example tf module comment to paste into PR body:
"Terraform changes: reboot strategy updated to rolling-with-warmup. Operator note: schedule off-peak 0200-0400 UTC, prepare fallback pool and warm cache. Link to runbook: CON-3421."

Escalation / pager blurb (for use in PD alerts or chatops):
"Priority: Sev3 (planned upgrade anomaly). Tenant: {{tenant_id}}. Symptom: elevated 5xx on upgrade. Visible since {{timestamp}} UTC. Current mitigation: traffic routed to fallback pool. Assigned: SRE on-call {{oncall_name}}. Next steps: assess smoke tests, consider rollback if error_rate > 2% for 5m. Links: PD:{{pd_link}}, Runbook:CON-3421, PR:{{pr_link}}."

Post-maintenance summary template:
Subject: Maintenance completed: {{window_date}} — summary for {{tenant_id}}
Body: Completed: runtime upgrade to {{release_tag}}. Duration: {{actual_duration}}. Observed: brief latency spikes at T+2m, 0.7% error uplift for 12m, no customer-facing data loss. Actions: cache warmup, telemetry validated. Follow-ups: schedule joint verification call if you reported issues.

Examples of comm cadence (recommended):
- T-72h: initial notice (concise + link to ops details)
- T-24h: reminder with expected impact and mitigation
- T-2h: final notice and contact details for on-call
- T+15m: quick completion ack (if green) or initial incident note (if degraded)
- T+24h: formal completion + metrics summary

Appendix: persona-specific phrasing hints (1-liners to swap into templates)
- Developer: "No code changes required; watch for transient 5xx and retryable errors."
- Ops: "Expect node drains and temporary CPU/GPU spool; monitor node-level telemetry."
- Legal/Compliance: "No tenant data exfiltration; logs/audit trail preserved and archived per KMS policy."

Notes on uniqueness and internal linking:
- This doc intentionally keeps messages short (1-5 sentences) so CS/SRE can rapidly customize.
- Attach the terraform annotation snippet to PRs so CS can surface the maintenance window in tenant dashboards automatically.
- If you use the PR title convention and the metadata tags above, the release automation can generate tenant notices automatically (see linked CON-3421).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add more localized time-zone variants for APAC customers (APAC-friendly windows and messaging).
- Add sample SMS/Slack short alerts for customers that prefer those channels.
- Confirm automation path for ingesting terraform "maintenance_notes" into the customer portal UI.

End of doc.
